hook.say: Be honest. Does every chai sutta break at the office, every house party with friends, end with the same question? Where the hell is all my tax money going?
hook.text: Be honest. Does every chai-sutta break at the office, every house party with friends, end with the same question… where the hell is all my tax money going?

three.say: Here's the thing. There are three Indias. India One: the ultra-rich. They invest, they create jobs, so the government listens. India Three: the underprivileged. They get schemes and subsidies to lift them out of poverty. And then, there's India Two. Us. The salaried, corporate crowd.
three.text: Here's the thing. There are three Indias. India 1: the ultra-rich. They invest, they create jobs, so the government listens. India 3: the underprivileged. They get schemes and subsidies to lift them out of poverty. And then there's India 2. Us. The salaried, corporate crowd.

pain.say: We pay up to thirty percent tax. We still pay for our own water, security and schools. And we get zero say, in how a single rupee is spent.
pain.text: We pay up to 30% tax. We still pay for our own water, security and schools. And we get zero say in how a single rupee is spent.

wishes.say: A jogging track in your neighbourhood park. E V chargers, because you're betting big on electric. Garbage trucks that actually show up. Or, India's own chip labs.
wishes.text: A jogging track in your neighbourhood park. EV chargers, because you're betting big on electric. Garbage trucks that actually show up. Or India's own chip labs.

meet.say: Meet निर्माण. Your tax. Your say.
meet.text: Meet Nirmaan. Your tax. Your say.

ninety.say: Now, not every rupee can be opened up. Defence. Interest. The states' share. That ninety percent, keeps India running.
ninety.text: Now, not every rupee can be opened up. Defence, interest, the states' share: that 90% keeps India running.

ten.say: But the debatable slice, could be decided by the people who pay for it. निर्माण starts with ten percent.
ten.text: But the debatable slice could be decided by the people who pay for it. Nirmaan starts with 10%.

start.say: Say you pay eight lakh rupees in income tax. निर्माण tears off your ten percent. Eighty thousand rupees, yours to direct.
start.text: Say you pay ₹8 lakh in income tax. Nirmaan tears off your 10%: ₹80,000, yours to direct.

browse.say: Browse projects in the city you live in, the hometown you grew up in, or across India. Back the jogging loop by your lake. Fast chargers for the nation. A library back home. And India's chip labs.
browse.text: Browse projects in the city you live in, the hometown you grew up in, or across India. Back the jogging loop by your lake, fast chargers for the nation, a library back home, and India's chip labs.

split.say: Split it however you like. No quotas.
split.text: Split it however you like. No quotas.

mint.say: Hit confirm, and your money is minted as purpose-bound e rupee. Digital rupees, that can only be spent on the project you picked.
mint.text: Hit confirm, and your money is minted as purpose-bound e-Rupee: digital rupees that can only be spent on the project you picked.

metro.say: Then, the best part. Watch your money ride the Money Metro. Wallet. Escrow. Agency. Vendor. Until your project goes live. Every hop, on a public ledger. Every milestone, with geotagged proof.
metro.text: Then, the best part. Watch your money ride the Money Metro: wallet, escrow, agency, vendor… until your project goes live. Every hop on a public ledger. Every milestone with geotagged proof.

pitch.say: Don't see your idea? Pitch it. Turn it into a campaign, share it with your society group and your running club, and rally verified vouches.
pitch.text: Don't see your idea? Pitch it. Turn it into a campaign, share it with your society group and your running club, and rally verified vouches.

loop.say: So when the government plans next year's budget, there's already a ranked list of what India's taxpayers want built. That's the feedback loop.
loop.text: So when the government plans next year's budget, there's already a ranked list of what India's taxpayers want built. That's the feedback loop.

govt.say: For the government, it means transparent governance, and the trust of the generation that pays for it.
govt.text: For the government, it means transparent governance, and the trust of the generation that pays for it.

you.say: For you, it's the pride of knowing you're not just paying for India. You're building it.
you.text: For you, it's the pride of knowing you're not just paying for India. You're building it.

edge.say: I know. It's a far-fetched idea, and you're probably already thinking of ten edge cases. Good. Shoot them my way.
edge.text: I know, it's a far-fetched idea, and you're probably already thinking of ten edge cases. Good. Shoot them my way.

public.say: I'm building this in public, and your feedback shapes what comes next. Try it. Break it. Tell me what you think.
public.text: I'm building this in public, and your feedback shapes what comes next. Try it. Break it. Tell me what you think.
